4 reasons why I don't like The Phantom Pain.

I feel like half of the reviews bitching about TPP are just people trying to be edgy by saying they don't like a popular franchise.

One of his major complains is that there isn't a codec? Really? Yeah, sitting there listening to dialogue is definitely more engaging than having Miller and Ocelot talking to you on the radio as you're doing things. MGS4 didn't really have a codec, either. Technically you have one, but it gets used like twice in the entire game. I always just thought of the codec as a handy means of exposition that saved a lot of work that would be spent on cutscenes.

Regarding Quiet... Did she really need to dress like that? No. Kojima admitted that part of the reason she was designed that way was because Metal Gear as a franchise hasn't really had much in the way of eye candy (Eva in MGS3 is basically it), and every good pulp-type espionage story needs a good hot-chick-that-could-totally-kill-you character. It's just a trope of the genre. Personally, I think the explanation is good enough (we don't ever get explanations for Psycho Mantis or anyone in the COBRA unit, so...) and also, Quiet is such a nauseatingly useful AI partner that she could be dressed in the Super Mario 3 frogsuit for all I care.

I have to admit that I'd greatly prefer David Hayter to Kiefer Sutherland, but I'd be more pissed if it was Solid Snake, as opposed to Big Boss. BB always seemed the more silent of the two, even in MGS3. The only person he really talks to at length is the Boss and possibly Eva. Whichever Snake, he definitely has a lot less to say in TPP than in any of the other games, but I see TPP as telling the story of the creation of Outer Heaven, rather than a single one of Big Boss's missions. It definitely has a different feel, but it works.

Sneaking past enemies involves a lot of crawling, and dispatching them in a score efficient way requires a tranq weapon because killing them is somehow less stealthy than giving them a quick snooze. The end result is that you spend most of your time on elbows and knees before aiming for heads with the knockout dart. At least that’s what it devolved into for me, and it’s gotten very old.

I started to feel that way around hour 35 or so... Until all of my mother base teams started to get really powerful. Once you unlock gas mines, sleeping grenades, vehicle-specific mines, the different types of decoys, get your c4 to the point where you have a TON of it... it felt like things opened up a lot more. Especially if you're using Quiet or D-Dog as buddies, who open up even more options. A fun combo I really like is a tranq sniper rifle + D-Dog with the battle dress that lets him extract guys for you. Or order Quiet to scout a base ahead of time, then start attacking before you get there. Sneak in while everyone's running around looking for the sniper. Or, if you really just feel like lighting someplace up, take D-Walker and spend an hour or two on a meaningless rampage.

And remember - you only have to worry about score in story missions, and that's assuming that you even care about what ranking you get. It's also possible to use lethal means/be sighted and still get an S rank. Your ranking is based on total score, not how how sneaky you were. Marking enemies gives you points. So does extracting. Headshots are worth more, particularly if you get one from outside the weapon's effective range. Speed is also a big factor. I've played story missions where I got frustrated with trying to be stealthy and do it correctly, so I just went on a rampage to complete it, and still got A and S ranks. It just has to be an efficient rampage.

I'll concede that the side ops can definitely get repetitive, but again, I feel like it is what you make it. I'll do an available side op if I'm close to it, even if it's one I've done before. It's a side op. A quick detour. Something besides the main story you can focus on for a few minutes. If the game forced you to do all of them, I think this would be a legitimate complaint, but otherwise... Then again, I thought getting all the Riddler challenges in Arkham Asylum/City was fun, so maybe that's just something I like about games.
